## Design

### 2026-10-27: Im starting to think that part selection is the single most important part of any project.

**4h**

Im starting to think that part selection is the single most important part of any project.

that's all I did today, I just picked out what components I want to use. battery life is the main limiting factor. I want to use a single CR2450 for powering this entire thing for pretty much an entire year, which sounds impossible, and it seemed that way when I was thinking like "oh I'll just use a pico and some tiny OLED display from adafruit" which would take like 80ma and deplete the battery in like 2 hours, but I think I got a configuration that works!

starting with the display, which was (fittingly) both the most critical and  the most power hungry. I started with an OLED display because I know they are slightly more efficient than LCDs, but then I checked the numbers and like I said earlier, that just absolutely wasn't going to work. my next idea was e-ink because it is ancient witchcraft that doesn't take any electricity to maintain the image, but it also has the refresh rate of a skilled artist which doesn't work if you want your animations to look passable. so, I did some research, and learned of this absolutely incredibly magic called a sharp memory LCD.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/0182a78988ec2d17cb7a89ab7416cac62bb62d4c05e8cb69217cc59d9e551a5a.png)

its like e-ink, but its also an LCD. witchcraft. unfortunately adafruits breakouts for them aren't in stock and I cant buy the raw displays except for one that is too big and from a sketchy third party retailer. so, I looked for alternatives. the liquid crystal dosent actually take that much power to run,  the back light is the real expensive part, but there is light everywhere, so why don't we just use that! this is how old power critical devices like the Gameboy and original tamagotchi work, and it looks awesome (as long as you actually have the light to see it)! but, I couldn't find any. everything was either too big, or too expensive, or too high resolution,  and I was much sadness and everything was horrible. but then I found her, the Crystalfontz CFAG12864U3-NFH.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/451430fc159fbfee88c4f008e11aedb464de5173619744d7fd6da982c0d6ddb2.png)

its perfect. bare SPI communications, integrated driver, 128x64 pixles, 56x42.5mm, and most importantly, 1-2ma while running. I couldn't have crafted a better display in my dreams.  also, what do you mean "transparent". you can have transparent LCDs? WHAT?  IS IT 2035?

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/23d52e9029f565397e64195c3ca065e1dcb93cabd23823bf4ad639d67bd3808b.png)

anyways there are also some other parts. for the micro controller I'm using a MSP430 because it sleeps like a baby and has a really convenient development board. also I want to shout out Texas instruments for putting their incredibly advanced high end chips in dip packaging for absolutely no reason other than allowing idiots like me to mess around with it on a breadboard. absolute goats.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/71df51822f38c73f42f910f8b1f27a883aa2b97dd87a9a41a10dea22a104874b.png)

and finally I spent to much time figuring out how peizo buzzers work, did you know the original tamagotich used a bare peizo filament connected to the case so the entire thing was a resonator? clever. anyways I'm not that clever and also I want this to be a bare board without a case because it looks cool, so I thought about using a bare filament so I could make fun frequency's also, but that was to much work for very little benefit over just stealing a buzzer from my school and putting it on 3.3v.

I also learned a lot about how to design the software for this, basically just put the entire thing in cryosleep for 99% of the time and it doesn't use any power, so now we do math!

a CR2450 coin cell has about 600mah. lets assume the display is on for about 10 minutes each day, about 0.007% of the time. 2ma * 0.007 = 0.014 ma. plus the  MSP430 which when sleeping (which is what it will be doing for literally 99% of the time that was not an exageration) 0.08 ma, so the whole thing is like 0.022 ma, 600/0.022 is like 27272 hours, Which is like 1100 days or about 3 years!

holy shit!

### 2026-11-03: ok so i made the schematic.

**6h**

ok so i made the schematic.

this week has been very very hectic for me, so I'm a little behind honestly, but im gonna finish this in like 2 days way before any reviewers actually look at this, so I you are a reviewer and you  see this feel free to send it back because I will have it done.  also I'm away from my computer right now so that's why pictures of the actual board are lacking, sorry :(

but anyways I made the schematic!  the first thing that took me way WAY to long was deciding what ZIF connector to use for the display. I ended up deciding on  this one, mainly because it was on digikey and no other reason.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/3051ebe3403af56429b415daa1fe7318e926057e292b76668f831898ce0ea74b.png)

then I had to decide on the exact micro controller to use (MSP430 is just a family) I wanted to use a DIP package one so that I can swap it easily between the programming board, and there is only a few options for that. BUT there are issues because of course there is. first of all it has 512 BYTES of ram. that's less than the Apollo 11 computer! you might also notice that if I have a 128 x 64 display, so I would need 8kb to fit a fill frame buffer. we don't have that kind of space! but, we don't need a full byte per pixel, we only need a bit. still, its now 1024 bytes, which is still way way way to big. but, I want it to have a stylish pixel art aesthetic, so we can also use that to save on performance by making a 64 x 32 frame buffer and scaling it up. that, with the 8 bit trick, makes it fit within 256 bytes, leaving a grand 256 bytes for the entirety of game memory. that's like 128 numbers. thats like a problem for future ian. anyways I ended up deciding on the msp430g2553in20 because it has a DIP package and also the most RAM of a DIP package.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/6a2979d28317477f259b31ec1d1dea140664e448d122fa3eff62a0f7baea5236.png)

actually I'm not sure why I added a picture it looks exactly like every other dip20 chip ever

also don't you just love the feeling of opening a pdf and having your life flash before your eyes

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/0d86472a5728005f507d213f5bcdeecc4bb6d1f739fdb9915c75bdc19fe5bc97.png)

this is why I make liberal use of AI to summerize things and point me to where the information is stated in the datasheet because there is no way I could read all 703 pages of that.

also what do you mean "family user guide"? who's family is using a msp430g2553in20? I'm getting distracted

PINMAPS. then I worked on pin maps. i misread the manual and I though it only had 8 GPIO pins, Wich is like barely enough to drive everything (3 for rotary encoder, 1 for buzzer, 4 for SPI) but I also wanted a pin to turn of the display, SO, I was gonna do this super cursed parasitic power setup where I have SPICLK and SPIDI connected to VDD via two diodes and a capacitor and then  I tie them to high when they aren't transmitting data and that is what powered the display, it was gonna be super cursed, but then I realized I was stupid and I had 16 GPIO pins.

I think thats all the interesting things? anyways here is the full schematic

![2026-11-01-114530_hyprshot](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/9dd126b42ef3475acb4338c3f90d0efda6593d986d2c36990599e4d037fbdf76.png)

I feel like an actual electrical engineer, with all the data sheets and the protocols and the decoupling capacitors and the milli amp hours, I feel so professional!

my next step is to do the layout obviously, but more importandly I need to think about *aesthetics*  wow  that made it italic basically I just need to decide what shape to make the board, surprisingly hard.

but for here its just connect the dots!

### 2026-11-03: you know how I said like 2 journals ago that the most important part of any project is part selection? well I was totally wrong the most important part is *asthetics* god I love markdown format

**4h**

you know how I said like 2 journals ago that the most important part of any project is part selection? well I was totally wrong the most important part is *asthetics* god I love markdown format

over the weekend I was away from my computer, so I took that time to have a good think about the artistic part of this whole thing. three main ideas stood out: flowers, gems. and space.

space was ruled out pretty fast. I love space and space themed things but I just don't think I have the skill or colors on a PCB to execute it. maybe when I get better at curcit board art I could make like a v2? I will probably end up doing that later maybe.
